record.oneLiner: A large, bulky iguanodontian herbivore with a spiked thumb.
record.description: Iguanodon was a large, bulky herbivore up to 9–11 m long from the Early Cretaceous of Europe, distinguished by large thumb spikes — possibly for defence — and long prehensile fifth fingers for foraging. One of the first dinosaurs ever named, it was among the three genera originally used to define Dinosauria.

notableFacts.text: Had large thumb spikes, possibly used for defence.
The second dinosaur ever formally named, and one of three used to define Dinosauria.
Superb complete skeletons were found in a Belgian coal mine in 1878.
